details:
SpectraX — Explore the Universe Through Time and Light

SpectraX is an interactive, science-driven astronomy platform that makes NASA's SPHEREx observations accessible, understandable, and explorable by everyone.

NASA's SPHEREx telescope observes the entire sky across 102 infrared spectral bands. SpectraX transforms this complex scientific data into an interactive experience where users can explore celestial objects, compare observations from different dates, investigate movement and brightness variations, and analyze infrared spectra.

How It Works

SpectraX retrieves real astronomical observations from NASA/IPAC's Infrared Science Archive (IRSA), including calibrated FITS images and spectral data. The platform aligns observations using astronomical coordinate systems, applies data-quality checks, and enables side-by-side comparisons, image subtraction, stacking, and time-based visualization.

Users can navigate an interactive sky atlas, explore 102 infrared channels, inspect spectral measurements, and overlay reference catalogs such as Gaia DR3 and AllWISE.

Technology and Innovation

We developed SpectraX using Python, FastAPI, Next.js, React, TypeScript, and scientific astronomy libraries, including Astropy. The platform integrates Aladin Lite for interactive sky navigation and processes real NASA SPHEREx data through a dedicated scientific analysis pipeline.

Our innovation lies in combining astronomical data exploration, multi-epoch comparisons, spectral analysis, and scientifically traceable measurements within a single accessible web platform.

Rather than presenting static space imagery, SpectraX allows users to investigate how the sky changes over time using real observations.

Scientific Validation

We tested the platform using five astronomical targets: Barnard's Star, Epsilon Indi B, WISE 0855, RW Aurigae, and R Draconis. These cases demonstrate motion measurements, brightness comparisons, and the importance of accounting for observational uncertainty and data-quality limitations.

Impact and Vision

Astronomical research data is often difficult for non-specialists to access and interpret. SpectraX aims to remove these barriers by making scientific exploration more intuitive, transparent, and engaging.

Our goal is to empower students, educators, researchers, and citizen scientists to explore genuine NASA observations, understand changes in the universe, and participate in scientific discovery.

SpectraX turns complex space data into an interactive window on our changing universe.
